chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, [from some of our companions], from Abu Sa'id al-Makari, who said:

We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he mentioned Zayd and those who went out with him. Some of the companions in the gathering began to speak of him (critically), so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) rebuked him and said: 'Wait? You are not permitted to enter into what is between us [our status and affairs] except by a way of goodness. Indeed, no soul from us dies except that happiness overtakes it before its soul leaves, even if it be the time of a camel's milk curdling.' He said: I said: 'And what is the time of a camel's milk curdling?' He said: 'Its milk curdling.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.فَوَاقُ نَاقَةٍ: The time it takes for a camel's milk to curdle, used as a metaphor for a very short duration

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'fawq al-naqah' (camel's milk curdling) mean in Shia hadith regarding the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cautions his companions against speaking ill of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that their spiritual status ensures immediate entry into paradise upon death. He illustrates the swiftness of this transition by defining 'fawq al-naqa' (the time for a camel's milk to curdle) as the brief interval between death and the attainment of supreme felicity, highlighting the certainty of their salvation.

en.basel-kadem: 38.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Abu’l-MIghra, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:
A gift is permissible, regardless if it is taken or not taken, divided or not divided. People, however, only wanted grants, and so, they were mistaken. A grant is not permissible until it is taken.
